# New-ZbxMapShape

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a map shape for the -Shape of New-ZbxMap and Set-ZbxMap.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxMapShape [-Type] <ZabbixMapShapeType> [-X <int>] [-Y <int>] [-Width <int>] [-Height <int>] [-Font <int>] [-FontSize <int>] [-TextHAlign <ZabbixMapShapeLabelHAlign>] [-TextVAlign <ZabbixMapShapeLabelVAlign>] [-BorderType <ZabbixMapShapeBorderType>] [-BorderWidth <int>] [-BorderColor <string>] [-BackgroundColor <string>] [-FontColor <string>] [-Text <string>] [-ZIndex <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A shape is a rectangle or an ellipse drawn on a network map, with optional text. The New-ZbxMapShape cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Shape of New-ZbxMap and Set-ZbxMap take as it is, alone or in an array. -Type is positional. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build a title shape and use it in a new map

```powershell
$title = New-ZbxMapShape -Type Rectangle -X 10 -Y 10 -Width 580 -Height 30 -Text 'Office network' -FontSize 14 -BackgroundColor 'DDEEFF' -BorderType Solid -BorderWidth 1 -BorderColor '336699'
New-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -Width 600 -Height 400 -Shape $title | Select-Object MapId, Name
```

The builder writes one shape hashtable (type, position, size, text, colours); New-ZbxMap sends it in -Shape. Colours are hex RGB without '#'.

### Example 2: Group elements visually with ellipses

```powershell
$shapes = @(
    New-ZbxMapShape -Type Ellipse -X 20 -Y 60 -Width 260 -Height 300 -Text 'Web tier' -TextVAlign Top -BorderType Dashed -BorderColor '009900' -ZIndex 0
    New-ZbxMapShape -Type Ellipse -X 320 -Y 60 -Width 260 -Height 300 -Text 'Data tier' -TextVAlign Top -BorderType Dashed -BorderColor '990000' -ZIndex 1
)
$null = New-ZbxMap -Name 'Data center map' -Width 600 -Height 400 -Shape $shapes
(Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Data center map' -SelectShapes).Shapes | Format-Table Type, X, Y, Width, Height, Text
```

-Shape takes an array; shapes are drawn under the map's elements and -ZIndex orders overlapping ones. -TextVAlign places the label inside the shape. -SelectShapes reads them back.
